title: Canary Collaboration Guild: Playbook (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for the cross-functional Canary Collaboration Guild — a lightweight set of rituals, decision heuristics, and checklists so product, SRE, infra, and model teams run predictable canaries/A-B rollouts for LLM-powered endpoints.

Context / why this exists (notes to self):
- We see repeated issues where a model change slips past functional tests but triggers semantic regressions in a subset of users, or increases tail latency under specific traffic shapes.
- Existing rollout docs are very focused on traffic slicing and metrics, but not on who actually coordinates the cross-team preconditions and comms.
- This doc focuses on the human + telemetry choreography for low-friction small-batch canaries.

Key principles (quick):
- Small exposure, fast observation windows, clear rollback criteria.
- Co-owned signals: product defines UX-acceptance, SRE defines infra/latency/error SLOs, model team defines quality checks/evals.
- Keep the slate small: one hypothesis per canary. No bundling multiple risky changes.

Guild roles and responsibilities (practical):
- Canary Steward (rotating): owns the plan, config, and runbook for the canary. Responsible for triage handoff if alarm fires. (Usually an engineer-product or platform engineer.)
- Product Owner (feature PO): defines success criteria for user-visible metrics and approves exposure size.
- SRE Contact: sets thresholds for infrastructure safety (p99 latency, error rate, resource saturation).
- Model Quality Lead: provides the prompt-set baselines, evaluation harness, and alerts for semantic drift.
- Communications Lead: writes the rollout blurb for internal comms and on-call page updates.

Pre-canary checklist (steward must confirm):
- [ ] Hypothesis stated in 1 sentence and linked to PR/Jira.
- [ ] Traffic slice defined (cohort size, filter criteria). Keep to <= 2% for first wave by default.
- [ ] Observability dashboard pre-baked (latency & error + semantic evaluation). Templates in Confluence page above.
- [ ] Smoke test plan + synthetic traffic generator ready (if applicable).
- [ ] Fallback model or routing path configured and tested.
- [ ] On-call rotation and pager escalation listed in runbook.
- [ ] Stakeholder notification scheduled (Slack + email + status page note).

Telemetry matrix (recommended minimal set):
- Infra signals: 5xx error rate, 2xx split, p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU/CPU utilization, queue length.
- Model health signals: semantic regression score (eval delta on production prompt set), hallucination rate proxy (user report volume or classifier), token-per-request distribution, output length drift.
- Product signals: CTR/engagement for the feature surface, retention cohort delta, user complaint thread volume.
- Business guardrails: spend spike (tokens/min, cost per minute).

Example gating thresholds (starting defaults — adjust per product):
- p99 latency increase <= +50ms (absolute) or <= +30% relative, whichever is smaller.
- Error rate (5xx) not exceed 0.05% absolute increase over baseline for 5 minutes.
- Semantic regression: automated eval delta <= -2% on critical prompt set OR any high-severity manual regression observed -> immediate rollback.
- Cost: token spend rate spike > 2x baseline -> investigate and pause.

Canary cadence (suggested):
1) Internal dogfood (0% external traffic) for 30–90 minutes.
2) Micro-exposure: 0.25% traffic for 30 minutes.
3) Small-batch: 1% traffic for 60 minutes.
4) Broad exposure: gradually scale to target (5–20%) with 2x time window at each step.

Decision heuristics (binary checks steward runs):
- Safety: any infra alarm or p99 breach -> STOP and rollback to last known-good model.
- Quality: if automated eval crosses threshold, convene model lead and PO; if high severity manual issues detected -> STOP.
- Business: if cost/run rate exceeds guardrail -> throttle traffic and investigate.
- If signals are marginal but trending, hold at current slice for +2x observation window and run targeted synthetic tests.

Communication templates (short):
- Canary start blurb (Slack): "Canary START: feature X -> model vY; cohort filter: 0.25% users (US web); steward: @Priya; watch p99, 5xx, eval-delta. Link: <dashboard>"
- Canary stop/rollback: "Canary STOP: rolling back model vY -> vX due to p99 breach AND eval-delta -3%. Oncall: @SREContact"

Escalation flow:
- Tier 1: Steward + SRE oncall (15 min window).
- Tier 2: Product PO + Model Lead + Eng Manager (30 min).
- Exec alert (rare): if customer-impacting or major spend > 4x -> Pager to Director+ and StatusPage incident.

Lightweight A/B variant handling notes:
- Only one behavioral change per variant. Keep variants named and pinned in rollout config.
- Use deterministic hashing where possible to preserve cohort stability.
- Store attribution keys for later slice-level analysis.

Operational runbook checklist (at start of canary):
- [ ] Bake dashboard (link in canary ticket).
- [ ] Notify stakeholders and create Slack channel with triage pins.
- [ ] Start synthetic users test for 15 minutes.
- [ ] Monitor infra and model health for 2x baseline window before exposing live traffic.

Common failure modes (observed):
- Model regression only visible on long-tail prompts -> need better production prompt sampling. TODO: add guidance for dynamic prompt-sampling job.
- Latency spike when KV cache miss rate increases -> track cache hit ratio per model variant.
- A/B contamination: variant leak due to caching headers -> ensure cache partitioning by variant id.

Open questions / TODOs (near-term):
- Define "semantic regression" taxonomy (minor vs major) and map to roll-forward vs rollback policies. (Owner: Model Quality Lead)
- Add an automated canary runner that will pause at gates and notify steward (investigate feasibility with infra team).
- Formalize how Dedicated customers' canaries differ (private deployments require additional compliance checklist).

Appendix: small checklist for low-friction canaries (one-pager):
- Hypothesis + Jira
- Steward & oncall
- Dashboard + alerts
- Fallback path tested
- Synthetic traffic run
- Slice size <= 2%

Notes to self: this is intentionally pragmatic and human-forward — the goal is to reduce decision friction so teams run many small canaries instead of few large risky launches.

Next steps (who does what):
- Priya: fold feedback from guild meeting (due 2026-02-25).
- Maeve: prototype dashboard template (due 2026-03-05).
- Lucas: spike on canary-runner feasibility and raise infra-PR (Jira ENG-4920).

(End of draft)
